cards.claim: GDT626 retains a four-grade inflectional or abbreviation slot as the strongest alternative to interpreting its terminal grade series as a numerical code.

evidence.quote:
The strongest countermodel is therefore not random spelling but a four-grade
inflectional or abbreviation slot. Its distributions really are conditioned:
value III among II+III is 0.821 in Herbal but 0.455 in Biological material,
and 0.840 for Hand 1 versus 0.608 for Hand 2. Value I is also line-final in
38/102 cases, compared with 368/3,404 value-III cases. GDT626 keeps that rival
alive. Yet conditioning does not contradict a numerical code: medieval
quantities and degrees also vary by content and scribe. The new reader is a
working default because it predicts concrete compounds that the pure
inflection account does not yet interpret.

cards.claim: qokaiin shaiin → hot degree III; moist degree III

evidence.quote:
## Concrete translation gain

The gain over the rejected generic prose is categorical. We no longer render
a line as “take material, do work, pass onward.” We can now recover bounded
claims with explicit values:

```text
qokaiin shaiin
hot, degree III; moist, degree III

chor daiin cthy
reproductive plant part: three measures; leaf material
```

The unknowns are visible rather than hidden: the exact plant term behind
`chor`, the unit selected by `d`, and the wider syntax around these clauses.
The next useful target is consequently `chol`, because it is the fixed
predecessor of every value in the only identical I–IV `d` frame. Resolving that
head can turn the current local amount phrase into a fuller ingredient or
record clause without reopening the already established value architecture.
